newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Marshall prepares for duel with old foe.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Marshall prepares for duel with old foe.

text.p: WELLINGTON, June 30 - All Black halfback Justin Marshall was a clear loser on points the first time he marked his next test opponent, Wallaby George Gregan, on the rugby field.

It was an occasion, he says, that he didn't enjoy. He vowed it would not happen again, and after several other confrontations the pair face up again in Saturday's Bledisloe Cup match in Christchurch with Marshall ahead by several rounds.
"He's a competitor, but I haven't gone too bad against him in the past," Marshall said of his in-form Australian opponent.
"I remember he outplayed me in the under-19s match between the two countries, even though we won the match.

"I remember that I thought... bloody hell, I'm never going to get outplayed by him again, so I've made it a benchmark in my game that every time I see his name in the programme opposite mine I'm determined to go out there and not be outplayed."

Marshall, in only his third run after a five-week injury break, was probably the best of the All Black backs against the Pumas on Saturday night. His sharpness is surprising considering his lack of play, but he knows Gregan will keep him up to the mark.

"I think I've basically managed to have the better of him and I'm going to be making sure I do well on Saturday. He's as much of a competitor as I am. We really get stuck into each other, and that's the way it should be.
"It's an intense rivalry. George is one of the very best halfbacks in the world. It's a big challenge for me."
Marshall is happy to have his Canterbury team-mate Andrew Mehrtens back for the Bledisloe Cup test, but he offers a very strong plug for Carlos Spencer's debut efforts as test first five-eighth.
"Carlos has been great and he's shown he can play test rugby. I've found it a pleasure to play with him in the past two weeks, because he's very lively and adds a lot on the field.
"It's great now that we have two very good test first-fives. I'm sure Andrew is aware of that. He's really keen to get back on the field at Lancaster Park."
